keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row, no Wikipedia article: 'Principality of Rostov' redirects to the Vladimir-Suzdal article). None of the pages gives an area or a boundary, only the town; the disc is the radius the three citing dossiers already use. Cliopatria draws these lands as Rostov-Suzdal to 1240, as the Mongol Empire 1241-1293 and inside Vladimir-Suzdal from 1294, so the renderer must give them to this state (the same overlap the Yaroslavl dossier flags).

ledger.note: 1219: Vasilko Konstantinovich takes Rostov as its own prince. Page: 'Prince of Rostov from 1219 to 1238', born in Rostov on 7 December 1209, son of Konstantin of Rostov, who died on 2 February 1218 (Konstantin page; 1207: 'Vsevolod sent him to rule the towns of Rostov and Yaroslavl'). The Vladimir-Suzdal page has Konstantin dividing the land after Lipitsa (1216) into 'three new appanage principalities', Rostov, Yaroslavl and Pereyaslavl, without a year for the division, so the page's year for Vasilko stands.

minus.text: the extent that the Tver dossier (tver.json, same author) claims for Tver: 'The principality stretched from Kashin in the east to Zubtsov in the west' (Principality of Tver page), drawn as Tver 75 km plus Kashin 45 km plus Zubtsov 45 km

region.text: the land round Rostov the Great that the 1375 and 1395 shapes share (12 cells); the disc is 40 km of mine, the pages give no extent

ledger.note: 1389: the Rostov lands pass out of the grand principality's shape. Page: 'by 1389, the two thrones were permanently united'; its sentence that the principality 'rapidly disintegrated into eleven tiny states' (which 'nominally acknowledged the suzerainty of the Grand Prince of Vladimir') belongs to the aftermath of the Mongol invasion, not to 1389 [reviewer g-eu-c 2026-11-01: wording corrected]. The page does not date any transfer of land; the year is the Vladimir-Suzdal dossier's loss of the same 12 cells (confidence 1), and Rostov itself was an appanage since 1219.

1474: Moscow absorbs Rostov. Ivan III page, annexations by 'conquest, purchase, or marriage contract': 'Rostov in 1474'; the Rostov Veliky page: 'finally incorporated into the Grand Principality of Moscow in 1474'.

notes: No Cliopatria row and no Wikipedia article of its own ('Principality of Rostov' redirects to the Vladimir-Suzdal article, which names Rostov only as one of the appanages), so the dossier rests on two biography pages (Konstantin, Vasilko), the town page and the Ivan III annexation list. Not on any page opened: the extent of the principality, its princes after Vasilko (his sons Boris and Gleb have no dates), any purchase of parts of Rostov by Moscow before 1474 (the Ivan III page mentions none), and the line of princes to 1474. The ruler strip is therefore omitted. Native names omitted (none on a page). The year 1219 is Vasilko's accession (page); 1207 is Konstantin's first rule of Rostov, 1216-1218 his grand principate. Cross-dossier match: the 1389 gain repeats the Vladimir-Suzdal dossier's loss (ledger 9, 12 cells, confidence 1) and the 1474 loss repeats the Moscow dossier's gain (ledger 32). Rostov is an appanage of the grand principality of Vladimir that the Vladimir-Suzdal dossier hands over only in 1389; the keyframe holds the disc from 1219, so the renderer must reconcile with Cliopatria's Rostov-Suzdal (to 1240) and Vladimir-Suzdal (from 1294) shapes that contain the same land. Gazetteer: place 'Rostov Veliky' resolves.
